patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 5 adds the abstract passage 78591240f49ebe53ec5e6e5c13598dc5 at item level to the frame shock mount port, shock upper mount port, shock-frame flow, and interface. That passage expressly states that the rear shock attaches to the linkage and frame. Claim 1 passage 99957d7f6c4eb694f7d5952940717ddd supports the two links, frame/link and swing-arm/link openings, mutual link openings, alternative shock opening, and progression range. The model does not assert which link is selected for shock attachment.

functional_completeness.rationale: Captures the claimed two-link architecture and mating mounting relationships, shock-to-frame context, shock-mount alternatives as unconnected optional ports, and qualitative leverage/progression behavior. Detailed geometry and application-specific configurations are appropriately omitted; model warnings acknowledge the uninstantiated alternative shock-link topology.

flow_consistency.rationale: All instantiated links are mechanical mounting interfaces with compatible mechanical_joint ports; references resolve to existing component/port/flow IDs and connections are recorded once. No incompatible transformation is modeled. Shock-to-link connection remains intentionally uninstantiated rather than imposing either disclosed alternative.

claim_traceability.rationale: Previously flagged shock-to-frame endpoints and connection now cite the abstract passage, which expressly supports the relation. ID-bearing model elements have item-level citations in the candidate; claim-level progression statement is supported by claim passage 99957d7f6c4eb694f7d5952940717ddd and calculation rationale by 6a2e639cae72218a86a7fc32ee20277c.

interfaces.rationale: Frame-link, inter-link, link-swing-arm, and shock-frame interfaces reference existing compatible ports and flows. Separate external frame, swing arm, and shock components avoid a generic EXTERNAL. Alternative shock-link ports are present without a falsely fixed connection.

textbook_application.rationale: Textbook context/interface guidance supports the modeling choice to distinguish external contextual components and avoid fixing application-dependent configuration; it is not used as invention evidence. The retrieved alternative-configuration textbook result was unrelated scoring guidance, so no invention claims are derived from it.

summary: Independent review of saved SJS 1.0 revision 5: no unresolved findings. The revision-4 shock-frame citation concern is resolved: the abstract passage 78591240f49ebe53ec5e6e5c13598dc5 explicitly says the rear shock attaches to both linkage and frame, and revision 5 cites it at the relevant shock/frame ports, shock-frame interface, and flow. Reviewed the cited claim, abstract, and calculation passages against the model; the two-link structure, mount interfaces, alternative shock opening, qualitative leverage behavior, and progression claim are supported. External context components and deliberately uninstantiated alternative shock-link topology are reasonable. No evident SJS reference or flow compatibility defects; omitted geometry is appropriately left unspecified.
